description:
Prove at the CLI that the event history commands read a log holding retired-tag records and omit those records, so this repository's append-only log stays readable.

## Background

The one domain parser, `domain::parse_known_events` (`crates/jit/src/domain/event_log.rs:42-80`), skips a well-formed record whose tag is not a current `EventTag` (`:66`). Both storage backends read through it, and a cross-backend storage test owns that rule (the in-memory event parser change 47a082ef). `jit events query --event-type` parses its argument into an `EventTag` (the event tag vocabulary change e98ae5a4). The history-reporting commands that parse the log are `jit events tail`, `jit events query` and `jit worktree store-divergence` (`commands/events.rs`, `commands/worktree.rs:347-348` through `storage/json.rs:76` `read_exact_store`). This repository's log holds retired-tag records (`document_archived`), and history is append-only, so they stay. No CLI test shows these commands over such a log; their existing tests live in `crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/integration_test.rs`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A CLI test plants a well-formed retired-tag record between two current records and shows that `jit events tail` and `jit events query` succeed and report both current records and not the retired one.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: History commands report a log holding retired-tag records
